name: California

context: CA 340: cover crops reduce sheet, rill, and wind erosion.
CA 603: herbaceous wind barriers apply on cropland where wind erosion is a resource concern.
cover_rules: CA 340: maximize canopy plus residue cover to a minimum of 90-percent cover during the period of potentially erosive wind or rainfall.
CA 340: include at least one fibrous rooted grass in the cover crop.
CA 340: broadcast seeding rates should be 1.5 to 2 times the drill rate.
residue: CA 589: crop residues are left standing and undisturbed by tillage through the critical wind erosion periods.
barriers: CA 603: herbaceous barriers need minimum expected height of 1.5 feet and porosity of 40 to 50 percent; spacing not over 10 times barrier height.
CA 589: trap strips at least 15 feet wide when vegetation is at least 1 foot tall, 25 feet wide when under 1 foot; angle 65 to 90 degrees to wind.
CA 588: crosswind ridges run 65 to 90 degrees to prevailing erosive winds; tillage set for maximum surface cloddiness.
windbreak: CA 380: species come from the NRCS eVegGuide or are approved by the NRCS State or Area Forester or Lockeford Plant Materials Center.
grazing: CA 528: plan grazing to keep adequate ground cover from canopy, litter and trampled residue to cut soil detachment by wind and water.
CA 528: annual rangeland minimum RDM is 300 lb/ac on 0-10% slope at 0-25% woody cover, dry grassland (under 12 inches precipitation).
drought: CA 528: develop contingencies for episodic disturbances such as drought.
seeding: CA 342: dune stabilization seed is incorporated not more than 1 inch deep; fertilizer 500 pounds per acre unless specified.
dunes: CA 342: dune plants must survive burial by blowing sand, sand blasting, salt spray, drought, heat and low nutrients.
CA 342: include sand trapping devices such as sand fences or brush matting.
CA 342: temporary wind barriers are laid out across the dune area before seeding and mulching.
